title: Why Are Tech Companies Obsessed With India?
summary: 了解科技企业在印度的投资、工程人才与人工智能布局。
text: SummaryThis video examines the expansion of major technology companies in India. It discusses investment, infrastructure, engineering talent, labor costs, visa policy, and remote work, tracing a shift from back-office services toward AI development. Watch on YouTube Content 以下为原笔记中的视频转录与学习内容，保留原素材的叙述语境。 Section 1: The Macro Trend & The Shift from US to IndiaImages like these of the world’s leading technology and AI leaders, alongside the Prime Minister of India, demonstrate how interested tech companies are in this country. It’s here in India where tech giants—including Amazon, Google, and Microsoft—have pledged to invest over $67.5 billion to deepen their AI footprint. It is estimated that in 2025 alone, companies like Google, Amazon, and now OpenAI have opened hundreds of thousands of job positions for workers in India. Look at India. LinkedIn has just released its AI labor market report for 2026, and the headline is hard to ignore: around 60% of AI engineering job postings are in India, marking the fastest growth among all major global markets. Meanwhile, in the United States, we keep hearing news about layoffs in the technology sector. Mounting layoffs across the tech industry are leaving tens of thousands of workers without many options. Just yesterday, we learned Meta is planning to cut 8,000 jobs, or about 10% of its staff. It’s just the latest in a wave of layoff announcements. Section 2: Infrastructure, Investments, and the Talent PoolMulti-billion-dollar mega-structures in some of India’s largest cities—such as Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—demonstrate how committed these companies are to expanding in this country. Google announced a massive project in Visakhapatnam. They will be pumping in $15 billion in the next five years for what? To build a massive artificial intelligence hub—an AI hub. Once completed, it will be their largest outside the United States. Since the $100,000 tariff on H1B visas came into effect, companis have hired around 250,000 employees across India. At a time when AI is expected to reduce hiring, some of the world’s biggest IT companies are actually hiring more people in India, and that is becoming a new global trend. Capgemini, Cognizant, and EPAM Systems have all increased headcount in India to drive growth and protect margins. What is concerning is that this seems to be a trend that is growing more and more. So, why are tech companies hiring again, but outside the USA? Section 3: Historical Evolution (From Back Office to AI Laboratory)Just two decades ago, India had become the “back office of the world.” While night fell in the West, thousands of buildings in India lit up to handle customer calls from the United States and Europe. In the early 2000s, more than 70% of global IT and business process outsourcing (BPO) passed through India, with giants like Infosys, Wipro, and Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) managing everything from technical support to payroll processing for multinational companies. In cities like Gurugram, entire towers housed call centers where a single complex could employ more than 30,000 people. After weeks of training, many of them adopted neutral accents and Western names to assist customers thousands of miles away. By 2010, the sector was already generating more than $100 billion annually and employing over 2.5 million people, becoming one of the country’s main sources of income. The fact that Transact Global has found success by serving largely its own market is an indication of just how far the market has come. India’s IT sector has evolved so far out of its call center beginnings that it’s now a $150 billion industry. India was not only participating in digital globalization; it was sustaining it from the shadows. The thing is, until then, India was a very basic tech hub with delegated tasks that were quite simple. But now, that seems to be changing. Tech companies have begun outsourcing the hiring of senior engineers to countries in Asia. Section 4: The Core Drivers—Cost, Scale, and the H1B Policy ShockThis shift is reflected in the massive investments in training and development being made by companies like Microsoft, which has committed $17.5 billion in India—its largest investment in Asia. Likewise, Google has pledged $15 billion for a new data center hub, while Amazon plans to invest $35 billion through 2030. And finding personnel is not difficult at all. It is estimated that each year, India produces around 1.5 million graduates in engineering and IT-related fields—a figure that by itself explains the scale of the phenomenon. Indian tech workers are a worldwide phenomenon, with 850,000 entering the global workforce every year. A primary source for this talent is the country’s 23 Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). They’re among the most competitive engineering schools in the world. This enormous talent pool becomes the engine that powers both tech giants and rapidly expanding startups, allowing them to grow at a speed that is difficult to replicate in other markets. To put it into perspective, the USA graduates only about 80,000 computer science engineers annually. This difference makes India a very attractive place for companies seeking qualified personnel at a low cost. The salary gap is enormous. While a software engineer in cities like San Francisco can easily earn between $120,000 and $180,000 per year—and even exceed $200,000 in large tech companies—in contrast, in cities like Bengaluru, a similar profile usually earns between $10,000 and $25,000 annually, with higher salaries of up to $40,000 reserved for senior profiles or global companies. “I shared my salary progression to making over $250,000 per year at Facebook, and the response was interesting to say the least.” It became clear that software engineers in the United States make an order of magnitude more money than those doing the exact same job elsewhere in the world. It is a gap of up to five or even ten times less for comparable talent, which explains why so many multinationals have moved key operations there. But relocating entire departments to the other side of the world is not an easy task. That is why many of these companies used to bring specialized talent to the United States. The H1B visa was the best way to do it, allowing companies in San Francisco or Seattle to hire highly qualified engineers from countries like India and relocate them to the United States. In 2024, about 400,000 H1B visa applications were approved; 65% of those were people renewing their visas. Tech companies dominate the program. The top companies with employees holding H1B visas include Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft. It’s estimated that around 85,000 new H1B visas are issued each year, although demand usually triples that number, making them a scarce and highly competitive resource. The H1B visa is a program that allows US companies to bring qualified personnel into the country with relatively few procedures. Giants like Google, Microsoft, or Amazon have relied on this system for decades to strengthen their teams with global talent. But in 2025, something changed. The administration of Donald Trump imposed a $100,000 tariff on each visa application, making it extremely expensive for companies that used it before. “We need workers. We need great workers. And this pretty much ensures that that’s what’s going to happen. I think Sean, you agree with that?” “Well, they’re $100,000 per year. So the whole idea is, no more will these big tech companies or other big companies train foreign workers.” According to the government, this measure was taken to discourage cheap, mass hiring from abroad and because it was believed that many companies, especially tech companies, were abusing this visa program. This made it no longer profitable for tech giants to bring foreign personnel into the country. Section 5: The Rise of Remote-First & Data DeregulationSo, they began to change their strategy. Since the introduction of this new cost associated with the H1B visa, the global talent map began to shift almost immediately. What used to be bringing engineers to cities like San Francisco or Seattle has now begun to transform into sending the work to where the talent is. Within months, many companies chose to accelerate outsourcing strategies, and regions like South America and Asia became key players. Countries like Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia began to attract projects that previously would have required relocation, driving exponential growth in exported tech services in several of these markets. Why pay double when you can get the same technical quality for less? That’s exactly why US businesses are hiring more Latin American talent than ever. It is estimated that spending on IT outsourcing services exceeded $460 billion in 2025 and maintains annual growth rates close to 12%. At the same time, giants like Accenture and Globant aggressively expanded their distributed teams, while India further consolidated its advantage with millions of available developers. But India is not only an ideal place for outsourcing due to its low costs, but also due to the lack of regulation. As a highly populated country with historically more flexible regulatory frameworks regarding data, India has, in many cases, ended up functioning as a real large-scale laboratory for the tech industry. With more than 1.4 billion inhabitants and over 850 million internet users, any product can be tested with a diversity of users that is difficult to replicate in other markets. India has the second-highest number of internet users in the world—more than double the US. This is largely thanks to the country’s vast digital infrastructure. India has more than 700 million smartphone users. It has access to cheap data. It has digital payment platforms and public identity platforms. That scale is unmatched by any other country. In terms of data storage and usage, India has historically offered a more permissive environment than the United States, allowing tech companies to experiment more freely. While in the United States, companies are subject to a complex web of laws that limit how long they can store personal data, how it must be anonymized, and under what conditions it can be reused, in India, it is quite the opposite. It is common for digital platforms to retain large volumes of user data for longer periods. Moreover, this data can be reused for algorithm training, intensive personalization, or testing new products—often without the same level of restrictions or oversight. This allows, for example, the training of artificial intelligence models with massive datasets of real behavior, from payment patterns to app usage, at a scale difficult to replicate in more regulated markets. The data generated by all of the Indians using their devices is massive, and that is a gold mine. There is not any other country that can generate this scale of data. Although new laws in India have introduced clearer limits and obligations, the country still offers, in practice, greater operational flexibility than the US, which continues to attract companies seeking to iterate quickly and at scale. Since the rise of artificial intelligence, India has once again become the preferred destination for Big Tech, but this time not only for simple tasks. Roles such as AI engineers and developers are skyrocketing. It is estimated that in 2025 alone, demand for profiles in machine learning, data engineering, and MLOps (AI Ops) in India has grown by more than 30%, far above Western markets. Additionally, an interesting phenomenon has emerged: remote hiring. Startups and Silicon Valley companies no longer need a physical presence to operate. In other words, they hire entire teams in India from day one. For decades, American companies have looked outside of the US to employ foreign workers at a fraction of the cost of their American counterparts. A recent article published by Axios sheds light on how some of these companies are not only outsourcing their jobs, but forcing the workers to train their foreign replacements. Global talent platforms and remote-first models have made it possible for a company to grow from 5 to more than 100 engineers in less than a year without leaving cities like Bengaluru or Chennai. This has led to situations where, in some cases, more than 40% of the technical team of US startups is already outside the United States, with India as the main destination. Likewise, companies have begun to go beyond traditional outsourcing. Instead of building large offices, they’re hiring remote talent working directly from home in India, further reducing operating costs. Maintaining a tech campus in cities like Bengaluru can cost millions of dollars per year in rent, infrastructure, and services, while a remote-first model can cut those expenses by 30% to 50%. After the pandemic, more than 60% of global tech companies adopted hybrid or remote schemes, and many took advantage of this shift to expand international hiring without needing a physical presence. Companies like GitLab or Automattic operate with globally distributed teams, including hundreds of developers in India working from home. Meanwhile, giants like Microsoft have maintained flexible policies that allow engineers to work remotely within the country. Up to 7% of their US workforce is going to be canned under this, all the while they have 20,000 employees in India. They’re cranking up H1B foreign visa worker sponsors and they’re cranking up their presence in India. This is not a layoff; this is not a buyout. I don’t care what Microsoft PR is saying on the branding—this is worker replacement at scale. In addition, platforms like Deel or Remote have facilitated this model, allowing startups to hire engineers in India within days. And the result is clear: companies are not only moving work beyond their borders, but also beyond their own offices, creating a global network of distributed talent. At Economy Media, your opinion matters to us. Subscribe and let us know what you think in the comments below. Vocabulary & Expressions这段文本是典型的商业新闻/科技评论纪录片旁白，使用了大量地道的商业、科技和政策术语。以下是核心亮点的深度分析： 1. 科技与商业行业术语 (Tech & Business Jargon) Deepen their AI footprint: 直译是“加深AI脚印”，地道表达为“深耕AI领域/扩大AI布局”。 AI Ops (MLOps): 人工智能运维/机器学习运维。AI模型开发、部署和维护的工程链条。 Protect margins: 保护利润率。在商业中，当面临高昂成本时，通过外包来“protect margins”是高频词组。 Business process outsourcing (BPO): 业务流程外包。即文中提到的早年印度代加工工资、接听客服电话的低端IT业务。 Sustaining it from the shadows: 在幕后默默支撑。比喻印度早期作为技术后台，不为人知但至关重要。 Data anonymization (anonymized): 数据去隐私化/匿名化处理。网络安全与数据隐私的核心概念。 2. 经济与薪酬对比表达 (Economic & Salary Terms) An order of magnitude more…: 高出一个数量级（即大约10倍）。这是理科和商业中形容差距极大的非常高级的表达，比单纯说 “much more” 专业得多。 Comparable talent: 同等水平的人才。比说 “the same good engineers” 更正式。 Fraction of the cost: 极小一部分的成本（九牛一毛）。 Canned: （俚语/行业黑话）被解雇/被开除。文中 “7% of their US workforce is going to be canned” 意思就是这部分员工要被裁掉。 Worker replacement at scale: 大规模的员工置换。说话者一针见血地指出，这不是单纯的裁员（layoff），而是用便宜的海外劳动力把昂贵的美国员工换掉。 3. 高级动词与地道短语 (Dynamic Verbs & Idioms) Pump in [money] / Crank up [presence]: Pump in: 注入/砸钱（如泵抽水一样源源不断输入资金）。 Crank up: 开足马力/大幅提升（原意是摇动曲柄发动机器，引申为加大力度）。 Hard to ignore: 不容忽视/极其显眼。 Shift almost immediately / Accelerate: 形容特朗普政府政策（10万美元H1B关税）出台后，市场反应的迅速与剧烈。 Iterate quickly and at scale: 快速且大规模地迭代（产品）。互联网大厂的核心生存法则。 中文翻译【引言：科技巨头的目光转向印度】诸如此类世界顶级科技与人工智能领袖与印度总理同框的照片，无不彰显出科技公司对这个国家浓厚的兴趣。正是在印度，包括亚马逊、谷歌和微软在内的科技巨头已承诺投资超过675亿美元，以深耕其AI布局。据估计，仅在2025年，谷歌、亚马逊以及如今的OpenAI等公司就已经为印度劳动者提供了数十万个工作岗位。 看看印度吧。领英（LinkedIn）刚刚发布了2026年AI劳动力市场报告，其头条新闻令人瞩目：全球约60%的AI工程职位招聘都来自于印度，增长速度位居全球主要市场之首。与此同时，在美国，我们听到的却全是科技行业的裁员消息。全美科技圈愈演愈烈的裁员潮，正让数以万计的员工陷入无路可走的境地。就在昨天，有消息称Meta计划裁员8000人，约占其员工总数的10%。这不过是近期一波又一波裁员公告中的最新一例。 【基建狂热与人才红利】在孟买、班加罗尔和海得拉巴等印度核心城市，一座座耗资数十亿美元的超级建筑拔地而起，足见这些巨头在印度的扩张决心。谷歌宣布在维沙卡帕特南启动一项宏大计划——未来五年内将源源不断地砸下150亿美元。为了什么？为了建造一个体量庞大的人工智能中心（AI Hub）。该中心一旦建成，将成为谷歌在美国本土之外最大的AI基地。 自从每张H1B签证被征收10万美元的“关税”政策生效以来，各大公司已在印度全境雇佣了约25万名员工。在全行业普遍预期AI会缩减招聘规模的当下，全球几家顶尖的IT巨头反而在印度逆势扩招，这正在演变成一种全新的全球趋势。凯捷（Capgemini）、高知特（Cognizant）和EPAM Systems等公司纷纷增加了在印度的员工人数，以此来拉动业务增长并保证利润率。令人担忧的是，这种趋势似乎还在愈演愈烈。那么，为什么科技公司又开始招人了，却偏偏要把岗位放在美国本土之外呢？ 【从“世界后勤办公室”到“AI前沿实验室”】就在二十年前，印度还只是“世界的后勤办公室”。每当西方夜幕降临，印度成千上万的大楼便灯火通明，开始接听来自美国和欧洲的客户电话。在21世纪初，全球70%以上的IT和业务流程外包（BPO）业务都流经印度。像Infosys、Wipro和塔塔咨询（TCS）这样的本土巨头，帮跨国公司打理着从技术支持到薪酬结算的一切琐事。在古鲁格拉姆（Gurugram）这样的城市，整栋整栋的大楼全被呼叫中心占据，单单一个园区就能容纳超过3万名员工。经过几周的培训，他们中许多人操着听不出本地口音的英音或美音，改用西方人的名字，为远在万里之外的客户提供服务。到2010年，该行业年产值已超千亿美元，吸纳了250多万就业人口，成为印度最核心的经济支柱之一。 外包公司Transact Global仅靠服务印度本土市场就能赚得盆满钵满，这一事实本身就说明了这个市场已经发展到了何种高度。印度的IT产业早已脱离了最初“呼叫中心”的低端形态，如今已成长为一个产值达1500亿美元的庞大帝国。印度不仅参与了数字化全球化，更是在幕后默默支撑着它的运转。然而在过去，印度还只是一个承接简单、派生任务的初级技术枢纽。 但现在，风向彻底变了。科技公司已经开始将资深工程师的招聘工作外包给亚洲国家。这一点从各大巨头在员工培训与开发上的惊人砸钱攻势中便可见一斑：微软已在印度承诺投入17.5亿美元，这也是其在亚洲的最大一笔投资；同样，谷歌承诺投入150亿美元建设新的数据中心枢纽；而亚马逊则计划在2030年前投资350亿美元。 而且，在印度寻找技术人才易如反掌。据估计，印度每年能培养出约150万名工程及IT相关专业的毕业生，单凭这个数字就足以解释这场浪潮的规模之大。印度技术工人已成为一种全球性现象，每年有85万人涌入全球劳动力市场。而这些才俊的核心摇篮，便是该国著名的23所印度理工学院（IIT）——它们是全球录取最严苛、竞争最激烈的工程院校。这个庞大的人才库成为了驱动科技巨头和初创企业快速扩张的引擎，让他们能以其他市场难以企及的速度狂飙。相比之下，美国每年毕业的计算机科学工程师仅有8万人左右。 【无法拒绝的薪酬差与签证风暴】巨大的资源差异让印度成为了那些寻求“高性价比”人才的企业的风水宝地。两地的薪酬差距犹如鸿沟：在旧金山，一名软件工程师的年薪轻松可达12万至18万美元，在大厂甚至能突破20万美元；反观班加罗尔，同等资历的工程师年薪通常只有1万到2.5万美元，只有顶尖的资深专家或跨国大厂的核心岗位，年薪才能达到4万美元。 “当我分享了自己在Facebook年薪一路飙升至25万美元以上的经历时，大家的反应可以说是意味深长。”事实很明显：美国软件工程师的收入，比那些在世界其他地方做着一模一样工作的同行，整整高出了一个数量级（近10倍）。面对同等技术水平的人才，这里能省下5到10倍的薪水，这恰恰解释了为什么如此多的跨国企业会将核心业务迁往海外。 然而，将整个部门搬到地球的另一端绝非易事。这也是为什么过去很多公司更倾向于把顶尖人才带回美国本土。H1B签证曾是最佳途径，它允许旧金山或西雅图的企业以相对简便的手续，从印度等国引进高素质工程师并安置在美国。2024年，大约有40万份H1B签证申请获得批准，其中65%是续签。科技大厂是该项目的绝对主力，持有H1B签证员工最多的企业正是亚马逊、谷歌、Meta和微软。据估计，每年新签发的H1B签证大约有8.5万张，尽管实际需求往往是这个数字的三倍，使其成为一种极其稀缺和竞争激烈的资源。 但在2025年，游戏规则改变了。特朗普政府对每份签证申请征收了10万美元的“关税”，让以往高度依赖该签证的企业直呼“用不起”。 “我们需要工人，我们需要优秀的工人。而这一举措基本上能确保结果如我们所愿。肖恩，你同意吧？” “是的，每年10万美元。所以核心意图很明确：不能再让这些科技巨头或其他大公司继续培养外籍员工了。” 据政府称，出台这项举措是为了遏制来自海外的廉价、规模化雇佣行为，因为官方认为许多企业（尤其是科技公司）在滥用这项签证程序。这直接导致科技巨头再把外籍员工引进国内变得无利可图。 【全面转入远程模式：换血，而非裁员】于是，巨头们迅速掉转船头。自10万美元的H1B签证附加成本推出以来，全球人才版图几乎在一夜之间发生了转移。过去那种“把工程师拉到旧金山或西雅图”的模式，现在变成了“把工作送到人才所在的地方”。短短几个月内，许多公司选择加大外包战略的力度，南美和亚洲地区成为了关键赢家。巴西、墨西哥和哥伦比亚等国开始承接那些过去需要员工肉身搬迁的项目，推动了这些市场科技服务出口的爆发式增长。既然能以更低的成本获得同等的技术质量，为什么要付双倍的钱？这正是美国企业比以往任何时候都更青睐拉美人才的原因。据估计，2025年全球IT外包服务支出已突破4600亿美元，并保持着接近12%的年增长率。与此同时，埃森哲（Accenture）和Globant等行业巨头也在大刀阔斧地扩张其分布式团队，而印度则凭借数以百万计的现成开发者，进一步巩固了其绝对优势。 除了低廉的成本，印度成为外包圣地的另一个原因在于政策的“灵活性”。作为一个人口众多、且数据监管历史框架相对宽松的国家，印度在很多情况下实际上充当了科技行业的大型“活体实验室”。这里拥有超过14亿人口和超8.5亿网民，任何产品都能在海量、多元的用户群中进行测试，这种测试环境在其他市场是无法复制的。印度的互联网用户数位居全球第二，是美国的两倍还多。这很大程度上得益于其庞大的数字基础设施：印度拥有超7亿智能手机用户，享受着极度廉价的流量，并拥有成熟的数字支付平台和全民数字身份识别系统。这种规模举世无双。 在数据存储和使用方面，印度历来提供了一个比美国更为宽松的环境，让科技公司能够更自由地进行技术试验。在美国，企业受制于错综复杂的法律网络，严格限制了个人数据的存储时长、如何进行去隐私化（匿名）处理，以及在何种条件下可以二次利用。而在印度，情况则截然相反。数字平台将海量用户数据保留更长时间是家常便饭。不仅如此，这些数据往往可以在没有同等审查和限制的情况下，直接用于算法训练、深度个性化定制或新产品测试。举例来说，这使得大厂能够利用最真实的国民行为数据集——从支付习惯到APP使用轨迹——来训练人工智能模型，其规模是那些身处严监管市场的同行们望尘莫及的。设备背后数亿印度人产生的数据，就是一座源源不竭的金山。虽然印度出台的新法律引入了更明确的限制和义务，但在实际操作中，它依然能提供比美国大得多的运营灵活性，持续吸引着想要快速、大规模迭代产品的科技公司。 自AI浪潮爆发以来，印度再度成为科技巨头的首选地，而且这一次绝非只为了应付低端工作。AI工程师和开发者的需求量迎来了井喷。据估计，仅在2025年，印度对机器学习、数据工程和AI Ops（运维）人才的需求就增长了30%以上，远超西方市场。 此外，一种有趣的现象正在蔓延：纯远程雇佣。硅谷的初创公司和成熟企业如今甚至不需要在当地设立实体办公室。换句话说，他们从成立第一天起，就在印度招募一整支完整的技术团队。几十年来，美国公司一直将目光投向海外，以美国本土员工几分之一的成本雇佣外籍劳工。美国媒体Axios最近发表的一篇文章更是揭露了一个残酷的真相：一些公司不仅把岗位外包出去，甚至强迫美国本土员工去培训那些即将接替他们的海外员工。得益于全球人才平台和“远程优先”模式的发展，一家公司在不到一年的时间里，足不出班加罗尔或陈奈，技术团队规模就能从5人扩充到100人以上。这导致在某些情况下，美国初创公司超过40%的技术团队其实身处海外，而印度则是最主要的目的地。 同样的，很多公司已经超越了传统的外包范畴。他们不再兴建奢华的办公大楼，而是直接让招募的印度远程人才居家办公，从而将运营成本压得更低。在班加罗尔这样的城市维持一个科技园区，每年的租金、基建和物业费用可能高达数百万美元，而“远程优先”模式能直接砍掉30%到50%的硬性开支。疫情之后，全球超过60%的科技公司采用了混合或纯远程办公模式，许多公司顺水推舟，在完全不需要设立实体分支机构的情况下扩充了国际员工编制。像GitLab或Automattic这样的公司完全以全球分布式团队的形式运转，旗下有数百名在印度居家办公的开发者。与此同时，像微软这样的巨头也保持着灵活的政策，允许工程师在印度国内远程工作。在这种趋势下，微软在美国本土高达7%的员工将被“卷铺盖走人”，而与此同时，他们在印度却坐拥2万名员工。他们一边在国内疯狂裁员，一边在海外加码外籍员工赞助、疯狂扩大在印度的版图。这不是简单的裁员，也不是什么企业回购。我根本不在乎微软的公关团队如何美化包装——这就是一场赤裸裸的、规模化的全球员工大置换（工人替代）。 此外，像Deel或Remote这样的全球雇佣合规平台更是为这种模式推波助澜，让硅谷初创公司在几天内就能合规地签下印度工程师。结果显而易见：企业不仅把工作转移到了国境线之外，更把工作送出了格子间之外，拼凑起了一张由分布式人才组成的全球网络。 在《经济学人媒体》（Economy Media），您的观点对我们至关重要。欢迎订阅，并在下方评论区留下您的看法。 整理自 English / Passage4。本页于 2026-09-28 整理发布。

title: Why are Americans' Finances Worse Than Ever?
summary: 讨论美国家庭财务压力、支出变化与经济环境。
text: SummaryThis video looks at the financial pressures facing American households. The notes connect everyday difficulty making ends meet with inflation, uncertainty, and wider economic disruption, and include vocabulary analysis and a Chinese translation. Watch on YouTube Content 以下为原笔记中的视频转录与学习内容，保留原素材的叙述语境。 “55% of people in the United States can no longer make ends meet. Today, the United States is experiencing a severe economic crisis where people feel that everything is increasingly getting out of control and they do not see a clear solution. The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment report is now nearing its lowest level ever, as years of sticky inflation and the lasting impact of the government shutdown loom large over American households. This has caused morale to be at one of its lowest points, as six out of 10 consumers see their financial situation becoming increasingly difficult. So the bigger headline is: we are awfully close to being as miserable as American consumers have been at any point in recorded American history. In addition, recent global conflicts have caused gasoline prices to rise by 25%, making it more expensive to live. Oil prices have soared since the US and Israel launched attacks against Iran, and gasoline prices have jumped $1 to $3.98 per gallon, according to data from AAA. Furthermore, tariffs have caused food prices to increase by 12%, forcing families to reduce what they consume in order to sustain themselves. Food prices went up by half a percent from July to August. That’s the fastest monthly increase since the fall of 2022, driven in part by commonly imported groceries. Wage stagnation also plays a key role, as wages are only growing by 3% annually. This leads many workers to rely on credit card debt to cover their basic expenses. Consumers are increasingly relying on credit cards to finance purchases of everyday goods and services, and that’s because they’re just getting a lot more expensive. All of this is leading the country toward an increasingly alarming situation where the economy and daily life could worsen if action is not taken quickly. So why are Americans’ finances worse than ever? The United States is going through an economic and social crisis that has affected citizens’ confidence and quality of life. In recent years, consumer sentiment has fallen by up to 30%, showing a very low level of confidence in the future. For example, this graph shows how consumer confidence in the United States has changed over the past years. In earlier years, the highest level was close to 135 points, while in more recent years, it has dropped to around 91, showing a significant decline. This change is not only reflected in numbers, but also in the way people think and act in their daily lives, as 6 out of 10 households believe their financial situation has worsened, reflecting a concern that continues to grow over time. As a result, many families must have two jobs to cover their basic expenses and make ends meet. So many of us do have to work two jobs to make ends meet. It takes multiple incomes to survive in this economy. On one hand, conflicts in other parts of the world have affected energy prices and created instability in the markets. Additionally, difficulties in transporting goods have reduced the availability of products in many regions. As a result, more than 200,000 jobs have been indirectly affected, showing that the problem impacts multiple sectors. These factors have created an environment of uncertainty that continues to grow and affects both families and businesses. The government shutdown is starting to show signs of worry in a lot of households, and there is a widespread decline in sentiment among political groups, population ages, and income levels. Many people feel that the economy will not improve in the short term, which influences their decisions. Currently, the level of confidence stands at 28%, reflecting constant concern. As a result, many families have reduced their spending and avoid risks. Consequently, 5 out of 10 people have reduced their essential purchases. This behavior also affects businesses; so far in 2026, more than 150,000 small businesses report lower income, limiting their growth. In this way, pessimism directly impacts the economy. Consumer spending is the number one engine of this economy. And if people are feeling bad enough about the economy that they start to pull back—maybe they don’t take that vacation, they don’t buy that car—there are going to be real economic implications. The conflict currently affecting the Strait of Hormuz has caused fossil fuel costs to surge. Currently, the price per barrel is close to $100, affecting different sectors. This increase is reflected in people’s daily lives. Transportation becomes more expensive, as do the products that depend on it for distribution. As a result, gasoline prices have risen by 25%, representing an additional expense for millions of citizens. For example, this graph shows how different costs related to energy and transportation have increased in recent years. Gasoline prices increased by about 36% and flight prices by around 7.1%, reflecting the overall impact. This situation generates significant concern. Many people feel that it is becoming increasingly difficult to cover their basic needs. As a result, 7 out of 10 citizens see fuel prices as a key problem, increasing the sense of instability. The thing that people don’t understand is that this will impact the price of everything. Everything we buy that is made with or transported with oil. And the longer this goes on, the more expensive it’s going to be. According to citizens, government policies have only worsened the situation. A survey revealed that only 20% of Americans believe that the government’s actions have been effective. This perception increases distrust and causes the population to question decision-making. The lack of visible results makes the problem seem harder to solve. Additionally, this situation also affects government workers. More than 300,000 employees have experienced delayed payments during times of crisis, creating concern in their households. This problem affects not only these individuals but also the overall functioning of the country. At TSA, roughly 50,000 officers will screen passengers without regular pay. Not being able to come home with a paycheck puts a toll on you—not only on your stress level, but on your spirit. Another important aspect of this crisis is the rise in food prices due to tariffs imposed in recent months. Currently, prices have increased by 20%, reducing the purchasing power of many families. This increase forces people to change their habits and prioritize spending. Many families look for cheaper options or buy fewer products. As a result, 6 out of 10 households have had to adjust their diet to maintain their budget. Additionally, this situation also impacts businesses. Restaurants and small businesses face higher costs and lower demand. As a result, more than 90,000 businesses report difficulties staying stable, reflecting the economic impact. According to a new report from the New York Times, the continued climb in prices forced at least one family-owned steakhouse to ‘declare a code red’. Wage stagnation is another factor that worsens the crisis. Although prices continue to rise, many people’s incomes do not grow at the same pace. Currently, wages have increased by only 4%, which is insufficient compared to the rising cost of living. This gap creates pressure on households as they must cover more expenses with nearly the same income. As a result, seven out of 10 workers believe their salary is not enough to maintain their standard of living. Additionally, this situation also affects consumption. More than 250,000 people report difficulties covering basic expenses, showing the direct impact on daily life and the overall economy. This means that a typical family of four needs to work more than two full-time, minimum-wage jobs to earn a living wage, and single-parent families need to work significantly harder. The increase in fuel prices has also impacted airlines. To avoid losses, many companies have had to reduce flights and reorganize their operations. This results in fewer options being available for users. As a result, ticket prices have increased by 18%, making travel more expensive for many people. This limits access to transportation and especially affects those who need to travel frequently. Additionally, more than 80,000 flights have been cancelled or changed at different times, creating further difficulties for passengers. As a result, five out of 10 travelers have decided to travel less, reducing overall mobility and affecting other economic activities. United is already cancelling nearly 200 flights tomorrow, Delta 170. And this is just the beginning, because these cuts could escalate to something like 4,000 flights daily sometime next week. The crisis in the United States is the result of several accumulated problems that affect both the economy and people’s daily lives. As long as there are no clear and effective solutions, uncertainty will continue to grow and public confidence will keep weakening. At Economy Media, your opinion matters to us. Subscribe and let us know what you think in the comments below.” Vocabulary & Expressions这段文本使用了许多典型的财经新闻、社会评论及日常采访中的地道英语表达。 1. 核心经济与社会词汇 Make ends meet (地道表达)：字面意思是“使两头相接”，实际指“维持生计”、“使收支相抵”。 例句：Many families must have two jobs to make ends meet.（许多家庭必须打两份工来维持生计。） Consumer sentiment / Consumer confidence (专业术语)：“消费者信心”/“消费者情绪”。这是衡量经济活力的重要指标。 Sticky inflation (财经术语)：“粘性通胀”。指物价上涨后，由于工资、合同等因素，价格极难回落的现象。 Loom large (文学/新闻常用语)：“赫然耸现”、“阴影笼罩”。形容令人忧虑的事情迫在眉睫。 例句…the lasting impact of the government shutdown loom large over American households.（政府停摆的持续影响正深深笼罩着美国普通家庭。） Wage stagnation (专业术语)：“工资滞涨”。指工资长期不涨或增长极慢。 Strait of Hormuz (地理名词)：霍尔木兹海峡。全球最重要的石油海运通道。 2. 生动及口语化表达 (Idiomatic & Colloquial Expressions) Awfully close to…：“极其接近……”。这里的 awfully 充当程度副词，意同 extremely，但语气更强烈、更带感情色彩。 Pull back：“缩减开支”、“往回收”。在消费语境下，指消费者开始捂紧钱包，减少非必要消费。 Put a toll on / Take a toll on…：“对……造成严重不良影响/摧残”。 例句：It puts a toll on your spirit.（这极大地消磨了你的精神/斗志。） Declare a code red (流行俗语)：字面意思是“宣布红色警报”。这里指“陷入紧急状态”、“拉响红色警报”，形容企业濒临破产或面临生存危机。 Living wage：“体面生活工资”/“基本生活工资”。不同于“最低工资”（minimum wage），它指能够维持一家人温饱、医疗、住房等基本体面生活所需的实际收入。 中文翻译 译文风格说明：本译文在保持原文数据准确性的前提下，采用了符合中文新闻专题片和纪录片配音的地道口语化风格。 55% 的美国人已经无法维持基本生计了。如今的美国正经历着一场严重的经济危机，人们觉得一切正逐渐失控，且看不到任何明确的解决办法。由于多年来挥之不去的粘性通胀，加上政府停摆带来的深远影响，美国普通家庭正笼罩在沉重的阴影之中，这也使得密歇根大学的消费者信心指数直逼历史最低点。 这导致民众的士气跌入了谷底，高达六成的消费者觉得自己的财务状况正变得越来越艰难。换句话说，更大的新闻其实是：我们现在距离美国有记录历史以来最悲惨的消费困境，仅有一步之遥。 此外，近期发生的全球冲突导致汽油价格飙升了 25%，生活成本水涨船高。自美以对伊朗发动袭击以来，原油价格一路狂飙。根据美国汽车协会（AAA）的数据，汽油价格每 gallon（加仑）猛涨了 1 美元，达到了 3.98 美元。不仅如此，关税还导致食品价格上涨了 12%，逼得许多家庭不得不缩衣节食以维持生计。仅从 7 月到 8 月，食品价格就上涨了 0.5%，创下了 2022 年秋季以来最快的单月涨幅，这在一定程度上是由常用的进口食品涨价所拉动的。 工资滞涨也是一个关键因素，目前年薪增速仅有可怜的 3%。这导致许多劳动者不得不靠刷信用卡来应付日常基本开销。消费者越来越多地依赖信用卡来购买日常商品和服务，原因很简单——因为这些东西变得太贵了。这一切正将国家推向一个越发令人担忧的境地：如果再不迅速采取行动，经济和人们的日常生活可能会进一步恶化。 那么，美国人的财政状况为什么会变得如此糟糕？美国正在经历一场触及民生与社会的深层危机，严重打击了国民的信心和生活质量。近年来，消费者信心指数大跌了近 30%，表明人们对未来的预期极度悲观。例如，这张图表展示了过去几年美国消费者信心的变化：早些年，该指数最高曾接近 135 点，而最近几年却暴跌到了 91 点左右，降幅惊人。这种变化不仅体现在数据上，更体现在人们日常的思维和行为方式中——六成家庭认为自己的财务状况已经恶化，焦虑感与日俱增。结果就是，许多家庭不得不打两份工来糊口、维持生计。 “我们当中有太多人必须打两份工才能勉强维持生计。在现在的经济形势下，单靠一份收入根本活不下去。” 一方面，世界其他地区的冲突波及了能源价格，造成市场剧烈动荡。此外，物流运输受阻也导致许多地区的商品供应出现短缺。结果，有超过 20 万个工作岗位受到间接波及，表明这场危机正在冲击多个行业。这些因素营造了一种不断蔓延的惶恐氛围，让家庭和企业都深感前途未卜。 “政府停摆已经开始让许多家庭感到焦虑，而且无论是在不同的政治团体、年龄段还是收入阶层中，悲观情绪都在广泛蔓延。” 许多人认为短期内经济不会好转，这直接影响了他们的消费决策。目前，消费者信心指数仅为 28%，反映出大家长期处于焦虑之中。因此，很多家庭开始缩减开支、规避风险。结果就是，有一半的人减少了生活必需品的购买。这种消费紧缩也波及到了企业，2026 年至今，已有超过 15 万家小微企业报告收入下滑，发展受限。可以说，悲观情绪正在直接反噬经济。 “消费是美国经济的核心引擎。如果人们对经济的前景感到足够糟糕并开始捂紧钱包——比如不出去度假了、不买新车了，这将会对实体经济产生真正的连锁反应。” 目前波及霍尔木兹海峡的冲突导致化石燃料成本急剧飙升。如今国际原油价格已逼近每桶 100 美元，重创了各个行业。这种涨幅直接反映在老百姓的日常生活中：物流运输变贵了，依赖物流分销的商品自然也跟着涨价。结果，汽油价格飙升了 25%，给数百万市民带来了一笔额外的沉重负担。例如，这张图表展示了近年来与能源和交通相关的各项成本是如何上涨的：汽油价格上涨了约 36%，机票价格上涨了约 7.1%，反映出全面的通胀冲击。这种局面引发了广泛的担忧。许多人觉得连最基本的生活需求都快无法保障了。结果，高达七成的市民将油价视为核心痛点，这进一步加剧了生活的不稳定性。 “大家不明白的是，这会影响到所有东西的价格。我们买的任何东西，只要是用石油制造或运输的，都会涨价。这种情况拖得越久，东西就会越贵。” 在民众看来，政府的政策非但没有解决问题，反而让情况雪上加霜。一项民调显示，仅有 20% 的美国人认为政府的应对措施是行之有效的。这种观感加深了民众的不信任，也让大家对决策层产生了质疑。由于看不到实质性的成效，问题似乎变得更加棘手。此外，危机还波及到了政府雇员。在危机期间，有超过 30 万名公职人员遭遇欠薪或延迟发薪，给他们的家庭带来了极大的困扰。这不仅影响了这些个体，也动摇了整个国家机器的正常运转。 “在机场安检（TSA），大约有 5 万名安检员要在没有按时拿到工资的情况下继续坚守岗位。” “下班回家却拿不到薪水……这不仅给了你极大的心理压力，更是一种精神上的摧残。” 这场危机的另一个重要方面，是近几个月因加征关税导致的食品价格暴涨。目前食品价格上涨了 20%，大大削弱了许多家庭的购买力。物价上涨逼得人们不得不改变生活习惯，重新规划消费优先级。许多家庭开始寻找更便宜的替代品，或者索性减少购买量。结果，六成的家庭不得不通过改变饮食结构（如少吃肉、买便宜食材）来勉强维持预算。此外，这种情况也冲击了商家。餐饮业和小企业面临着成本上升和需求下滑的双重夹击。结果，有超过 9 万家商户报告难以维持经营。据《纽约时报》的一份最新报道，物价的持续攀升甚至逼得至少一家家族经营的牛排馆不得不“拉响红色警报”（濒临破产）。 工资滞涨则是让危机进一步恶化的罪魁祸首。尽管物价在飞涨，但许多人的收入却根本跟不上物价上涨的步伐。目前，工资仅增长了 4%，面对高昂的生活成本无异于杯水车薪。这种收入与支出的巨大缺口让家庭承受了极大的压力，因为他们必须用几乎没变的收入去支付变贵了的各种开销。结果，有七成的劳动者认为自己的薪水已经无法维持原有的生活水平。此外，这也直接打击了消费市场。超过 25 万人表示连基本生活开销都难以应付，足见危机对日常生活和宏观经济的直接冲击。 “这意味着，一个典型的四口之家需要打两份以上全职的‘最低工资’工作，才能赚够维持基本生活的体面收入；而单亲家庭要想撑下去，难度还要翻倍。” 油价的上涨同样重创了航空业。为了避免亏损，许多航空公司不得不削减航班并重组运营，导致旅客的出行选择变少。结果，机票价格上涨了 18%，让很多人觉得出门旅游成了奢侈。这限制了人们的出行，尤其严重影响了那些需要频繁出差或探亲的人。此外，在不同时期已有超过 8 万架次航班被取消或调整，给旅客出行带来了极大的不便。结果，有一半的旅客决定减少出行，这降低了社会的整体流动性，也连带影响了其他经济活动。 “美联航明天就已经取消了近 200 架次航班，达美航空取消了 170 架次。而这仅仅是个开始，因为到了下周的某个时候，这种削减可能会升级到每天取消近 4000 架次。” 美国的这场危机是诸多长期积累的深层次问题共同作用的结果，它既重创了宏观经济，也深深刺痛了普通人的日常生活。只要一天拿不出清晰且行之有效的解决方案，这种迷茫与恐慌就会继续蔓延，而公众对未来的信心也终将消磨殆尽。 “这里是《经济媒体》（Economy Media），您的观点对我们至关重要。欢迎订阅我们，并在下方评论区留下您的看法。” 整理自 English / Passage3。本页于 title: Why Women Are Choosing Blue-Collar Jobs Over College
summary: 了解女性选择技术工种的原因、机会与职场障碍。
text: SummaryThis video explores why more women are considering skilled trades as an alternative to college. It discusses labor shortages, practical training, pay, and work that is difficult to automate, while also examining discrimination and unequal opportunities on construction sites. Watch on YouTube Content 以下为原笔记中的视频转录与学习内容，保留原素材的叙述语境。 More women than ever are choosing blue-collar jobs. Well, a number of factors are driving the trend of more women entering blue-collar work, including companies broadening their recruiting efforts in a tight labor market. “There are also better jobs available to women now — better-paying jobs — and they’re recognizing they won’t be alone in those careers.” As of 2025, only 3.5% of electricians and 3.1% of plumbers and carpenters are women. However, the number of women working as electricians in the United States has increased over the past two decades, and the number of women working as carpenters has increased by 17% over the same period. These jobs seem more secure because they require human skills that are difficult for AI to replace. “So the reason why I chose the engineering environment and construction in general is because that made me realize, when I was choosing my career path, that’s something AI won’t take over.” However, the demand for workers in these positions has also led women to pursue these jobs. “You have major industries in this country which cannot find people. For women especially, that creates opportunities for employment growth and rising salaries.” In addition, these jobs are experiencing wage growth. For example, a female plumber earns around $60,000 per year. Since 2019, average starting salaries for skilled workers have risen more than 25%, from $18.70 an hour in 2019 to $23.43 an hour in 2025. What once seemed like jobs only for men are now becoming attractive to women due to financial pressures and the rise of AI. So why are women choosing blue-collar jobs? In recent years, the construction industry and technical trades have begun to face a growing problem that threatens their development. Many workers with years of experience are reaching retirement age, leaving vacancies that are not easily filled. It is estimated that more than 25% of the construction workforce will retire in the next decade, raising concerns about who will continue this work. At the same time, cities continue to grow and require more housing, roads, and basic services, increasing pressure on this sector. In addition, the advancement of artificial intelligence is changing the way people work in many areas. Many companies are cutting costs by trimming middle management and, in certain industries, eliminating entry-level roles that can be replaced by AI. Nearly 40% of office jobs could be replaced or modified by automated systems in the coming years. As a result, many people are looking for safer and more stable jobs. This has led technical trades to be seen as a reliable option because they depend more on human labor. However, the sector also faces significant obstacles. Low female participation and certain cultural barriers limit the number of people who can enter, worsening the labor shortage. “We have a disproportionate experience of harassment and discrimination against women on construction sites. Women often end up on these sites as apprentices and are not given the opportunities to learn the broad base of skills that their male counterparts are able to learn.” One of the most relevant aspects of technical jobs is that they are difficult to automate. Unlike office jobs, these roles require manual skills, the use of tools, and direct interaction with the physical environment. This makes it difficult to replace workers with machines. Currently, less than 10% of construction tasks can be fully automated. Each project has different conditions and presents problems that must be solved in real time, requiring constant adaptation. In fact, two out of every six activities require the direct presence of a person to be completed correctly. This demonstrates that human labor remains essential. Additionally, the sector performs more than 300 million tasks per year, reflecting its importance to the economy and daily life. The combination of technical skills and problem-solving ensures that these jobs remain essential even in an increasingly automated world. “Experts say it will be a while before robotics can do the intricate work involved in trades like plumbing.” Another important aspect is that technical jobs offer economic stability. The shortage of workers has led to rising wages in recent years, improving the living conditions of those in this sector. For example, this graph shows the increase in wages in one of the most in-demand manual jobs in the United States. As early as 2005, the average salary of an electrician was around $45,000 per year. Today, that value has grown significantly, nearly doubling in some cases. Incomes have grown 15% above inflation, improving purchasing power. This makes these jobs attractive for those seeking stability without spending many years studying. In addition, the training time is shorter than in many other professions. This allows people to start working and earning money more quickly. In fact, six out of ten workers achieve economic stability faster than in traditional careers. It is also important to consider that the economic activity generated by this sector exceeds $500 million, highlighting its importance to national growth. These types of jobs allow women to advance professionally through practical experience, offering long-term security for workers like Jerry Lee, who bypass traditional colleges. They are physically demanding, yet stable and high-paying career options. Despite these advantages, the sector faces a serious problem due to the lack of workers. Many employees are retiring, and there are not enough new workers to replace them. It is estimated that more than 500,000 new workers are needed each year to maintain the current pace of activity. This shows that the shortage is significant and cannot be ignored. However, many people still do not consider these jobs a professional option, partly due to prejudices about manual labor. As a result, only 30% of vacancies are filled on time. This causes delays in important projects and increases construction costs. In fact, four out of eight companies face project delays due to difficulties in finding qualified workers. “They are saying, ‘We cannot find the workers we need,’ and that, in turn, affects not only the quality of construction, but also how long construction takes.” Low female participation also limits the sector’s growth. Although interest among women has increased, their presence remains low. Currently, less than 4% of the construction workforce is made up of women. Women often do not receive the same opportunities as men to participate in key technical tasks, which limits their professional development. It is estimated that more than 200,000 positions could be filled by women if better access and retention conditions existed. Additionally, one in three women consider the work environment a factor that makes it difficult to remain in the sector. This shows that it is not only about opening doors, but also about ensuring adequate conditions to stay and grow. “Get into the union and you can make six figures or better. It completely changes a woman’s life. We tell women not only are you going to get raises, but you’re going to know when those raises come, so you can anticipate when you’ll be making enough money to buy a home.” In response to this situation, technical training programs have become an effective solution. These programs allow people to learn while working, making it easier to enter the sector. On average, more than 70% of participants obtain certification in a short time. This helps them enter the labor market quickly and improve their skills. In addition, more than 300,000 people participate in these programs each year, demonstrating their growing importance. In comparison, 75% of graduates secure stable jobs shortly after completing their training. For example, this graph compares university graduates who find jobs versus graduates of skilled trade programs. In 2010, only 60% of university graduates found employment, while technical graduates reached close to 50%. This model efficiently combines practical experience and theoretical learning, better responding to current labor market needs and reducing dependence on long and costly education paths. “It’s all of the above, actually. What we need are young people coming out of high school going into technical jobs. Sometimes it’s a two-year degree. We also need current workers to upgrade their skills.” The shortage of workers in the technical and construction sector not only affects the industry, but also the economy as a whole. It delays important projects and limits the development of infrastructure necessary for daily life. It also creates indirect effects on other sectors that depend on construction and technical services. On the other hand, increasing female participation could generate a significant economic impact. It is estimated that this could increase GDP by 10% due to higher purchasing power and greater workforce participation. Additionally, the economic impact of this inclusion could exceed $600 million in different scenarios. For this reason, 90% of economies that promote labor inclusion achieve better results in sustained growth. This demonstrates that addressing this issue can benefit everyone. “And so we really do need to be looking outside of our state’s borders and outside of our nation’s borders to help identify how we can recruit workers to fill the jobs that we have available.” The shortage of workers in the technical and construction sector is a growing problem that affects both the economy and societal development. Furthermore, including more women and providing specialized training can be key strategies to overcome this crisis and strengthen long-term economic development. “At Economy Media, your opinion matters to us. Subscribe and let us know what you think in the comments below.” 整理自 English / Passage 2。本页于 2026-09-28 整理发布。

title: The (Overdue) Collapse of Windows 11
summary: 围绕 Windows 11 的产品变化、使用体验与争议展开讨论。
text: SummaryThis video examines frustration with Windows 11 through the relationship between users and the platform. The notes cover hardware requirements, online accounts, advertising, subscriptions, AI features, and privacy, with user control and trust as the central themes. Watch on YouTube Content 以下为原笔记中的视频转录与学习内容，保留原素材的叙述语境。 In 2026, millions of computer users still use Windows 10, even though Windows 11 has been available for more than three years. Today, there are more than 1.3 billion devices running Windows 10 worldwide on a monthly basis. But this is because several users began to notice that their system no longer felt like their own, but rather like a showcase full of advertisements and unsolicited notifications. Microsoft has basically been systematically exerting dominance over its users, to the point that you question whether your machine is yours, or if it is Microsoft’s and you’re just paying for it. It is estimated that more than 46% of devices worldwide were left without official support for Windows 11 because they required a new chip that many computers did not have, with Microsoft consigning millions of PCs to the ash heaps of history well before their time, all because of new TPM and security requirements. At the same time, the system began to display recommendations and promotions even on devices where a full license had been purchased. These little pop-ups will appear for local account users and will mention all the free services you can get if you log in with a Microsoft account. In turn, Microsoft allocated millions of dollars to its artificial intelligence partnership, prioritizing the increase of its market value rather than focusing on the user. The tech behemoth, the world’s second most valuable company, says it plans to invest $30 billion into UK artificial intelligence infrastructure by 2028. The problems do not stop, and more and more users feel trapped in a system that disappoints them. So why is Windows 11 failing so horribly wrong? For decades, Windows was considered the dominant operating system in the world of personal computers. For example, in 2015, it reached nearly 90% market share in desktop computers, which made it the almost undisputed standard in homes, offices, and educational centers. However, over the years, Microsoft’s strategy changed profoundly, shifting from selling products to prioritizing services and subscriptions. In 2023, its cloud service revenue exceeded $110 billion and represented nearly a quarter of the company. “Azure cloud growth again, another beat here — 40% growth year-over-year compared to expectations of 38.2%.” This change not only modified the business model, but also the everyday experience of the home user. Windows 11 stopped being perceived solely as software installed on a device. It became a platform connected to external services, with online accounts and the cloud as its central access. According to recent reports, more than 70% of Microsoft’s revenue comes from services, cloud, and subscriptions — not from traditional licenses. What was once a relatively neutral tool began to integrate into an ecosystem designed to generate recurring revenue and collect usage data. This opened the debate about whether the system still prioritizes privacy and performance, or if it now puts profitability first. These changes have made a lot of people wonder: Is Windows still a tool for the user, or is it a cash extraction exercise for Microsoft? One of the first symptoms of this transformation was the shift toward recurring revenue through subscriptions. At the beginning of the last decade, more than 50% of the company’s revenue came directly from traditional software licenses. This led to the proportion tilting toward connected digital services 10 years later. Moreover, the increasing requirement to use an online account is another central point of controversy. In recent versions, the installation process almost forces users to sign in with an online account, making the local account option less visible. In certain markets, 100% of standard configurations guide users first toward online authentication before allowing other alternatives. This results in each session being linked to external services, which facilitates synchronization but also expands data collection. It is estimated that more than 1 billion devices are linked to accounts within the company’s ecosystem, turning each use into a potential digital record. “Because you’re not just using Windows — Windows is using you.” But this isn’t the first channel to tell you that Windows is stealing your data, and it definitely won’t be the last. Everything you do on Windows is being tracked. Another issue that emerged among users was the implementation of the TPM chip, which marked a turning point in public perception. Also called the Trusted Platform Module, this chip serves to improve device security by protecting keys, passwords, and sensitive data at the hardware level. It comes integrated in most computers manufactured approximately from 2016 onward. However, although it was said to be for security reasons, in practice it left about 240 million computers without support, even though they were still functioning properly. Many of these devices could run office tasks, browsing, and studying without issues. After the announcement of the new requirements, the global personal computer market recorded sales increases of nearly 15% in the following period. For millions of people, especially in less-resourced regions, it meant choosing between buying a new device or staying without updates and assuming greater risks. “It will tell you this computer can’t run Windows 11, and even though it doesn’t exactly tell you why, a lot of people are confused about this. For the most part, it’s down to not having one of these TPM modules.” Another important point is that Microsoft began to strongly invest in AI. The company allocated around $13 billion to its partnership with OpenAI, placing artificial intelligence at the center of its digital ecosystem. As a result, traditional tools began incorporating automated assistance, text generation, and predictive suggestions across multiple applications. However, in recent studies, five out of 10 users indicated that they do not regularly use these advanced features. Even so, the constant AI buttons and notifications changed the visual experience and system functionality, disrupting user interaction. “As we lost the functionality and the clean UI, in exchange we got useless news and weather tabs, along with mandatory AI.” Another of the most controversial cases was the Recall feature, created to periodically capture on-screen activity and facilitate later searches. Depending on daily use, this tool can generate thousands of screenshots in a single day, creating an extremely detailed historical archive. Cybersecurity experts warn that databases of such magnitude constitute attractive targets for cyberattacks. For example, recent global reports show that more than 70% of serious incidents involve local information that ends up being exploited by malware. This has led users to not feel completely protected, since this could lead to a failure that might expose personal data. Security researchers later found that the way Recall stored data was not fully protected and could be accessed by malware or anyone with local access. Users no longer feel secure with the Windows 11 system, and this has led to a gradual migration toward alternative systems. Although Windows remains dominant, Linux-based distributions represent around 2% of the global desktop market. This equals millions of active devices. Additionally, after changes in hardware requirements, some communities saw up to 30% more downloads of alternative systems. For example, macOS maintains around 8% market share in developed markets, being an option for those seeking closed integration and fewer ads. While these figures do not represent a massive abandonment, they do show a progressive shift of advanced users seeking greater control. In 2020, Windows had almost 83% market share by unit shipments, while ChromeOS had 10% and macOS had 7%. The evolution of Windows 11 reflects a tension between technological innovation and a business model oriented toward data and services. More than 1.4 billion devices worldwide still use some version of Windows, making each strategic decision a global-scale phenomenon. However, in recent surveys, four out of 10 users said they are concerned about the information collected by their modern operating systems. This shows that privacy has become a central issue in the digital debate. Windows has always collected some information in the background, but over the years, that quiet data collection grew into something that people could no longer ignore. The Windows 11 crisis is not only technical or aesthetic, but also a transformation in the relationship between user and platform. If the focus continues to be monetization and data collection, public perception could worsen over time. On the other hand, if local performance, transparency, and real choice are prioritized again, the system could regain part of the lost trust — the trust that made Windows the almost absolute standard of personal computing for decades.
